# 2 Samuel Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 189v–190v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_018_page_001.jpg, 2SA_018_page_002.jpg, 2SA_018_page_003.jpg

---

**18:1** And-mustered David the-people who [were] with-him, and-set over-them commanders of-thousands and-commanders of-hundreds.

**18:2** And-sent David the-people — the-third under-[the]-hand of-Yo'av, and-the-third under-[the]-hand of-Avishai son of-Tseruyah, brother of-Yo'av, and-the-third under-[the]-hand of-Ittai the-Gitti. And-said the-king to the-people, "Going-out I-will-go-out [yatso etse], also I, with-you."

**18:3** And-said the-people, "You-shall-not go-out! For if fleeing we-flee [nos nanus], they-will-not set [their]-heart upon-us, and-if half-of-us die, they-will-not set [their]-heart upon-us. For now [there are] like-us ten-thousand. And-now, [it is]-better that you-be to-us from-[the]-city a-help [le'ezer]."

**18:4** And-said the-king to-them, "What is-good in-your-eyes I-will-do." And-stood the-king beside the-gate, and-all the-people went-out by-hundreds and-by-thousands.

**18:5** And-commanded the-king Yo'av and-Avishai and-Ittai, saying, "Deal-gently [le'at] for-me [li] with-the-youth [la-na'ar], with-Avshalom." And-all the-people heard when-the-king commanded all the-commanders concerning Avshalom.

**18:6** And-went-out the-people to-the-field to-meet Yisra'el, and-was the-battle in-[the]-forest of-Ephrayim.

**18:7** And-were-struck-down [vayyinnagphu] there the-people of-Yisra'el before [the]-servants of-David, and-was there the-slaughter great on-that day — twenty thousand.

**18:8** And-was there the-battle scattered [naphatsot] over-[the]-face of-all the-land, and-the-forest consumed-more [vayyerev] to-devour among-the-people than [those]-whom the-sword consumed on-that day.

**18:9** And-met [vayyiqqare'] Avshalom before [the]-servants of-David. And-Avshalom [was]-riding upon the-mule, and-came the-mule under [the]-tangled-branches of-the-oak [ha-elah] the-great, and-was-caught [vayyechezeq] his-head in-the-oak, and-he-was-given [vayyinnathen] between the-heavens and-between the-earth, and-the-mule that [was] under-him passed-on.

**18:10** And-saw one man and-told Yo'av and-said, "Behold, I-saw Avshalom hanging [talui] in-the-oak."

**18:11** And-said Yo'av to-the-man who-told him, "And-behold, you-saw, and-why did-you-not strike-him there to-the-ground? And-upon-me to-give to-you ten of-silver and-one belt [chagor]."

**18:12** And-said the-man to Yo'av, "And-if I [were]-weighing upon my-palms a-thousand of-silver, I-would-not stretch-out my-hand against [the]-son of-the-king. For in-our-ears the-king commanded you and-Avishai and-Ittai, saying, 'Guard [shimru] for-me [li] the-youth [ba-na'ar], Avshalom.'

**18:13** Or I-would-have-done against-my-life [nephesh] falsehood [sheqer] — and-no thing is-hidden from the-king — and-you yourself would-have-stood-aloof [tityatstsev]."

**18:14** And-said Yo'av, "Not so will-I-wait before-you." And-he-took three staves [shevatim] in-his-palm and-thrust-them [vayyitqa'em] in-[the]-heart of-Avshalom while-he [was]-still alive in-[the]-heart of-the-oak.

**18:15** And-surrounded [vayyassobbu] ten youths, armor-bearers of-Yo'av, and-struck Avshalom and-killed-him.

**18:16** And-blew Yo'av on-the-shofar, and-the-people returned from pursuing after Yisra'el, for Yo'av restrained the-people.

**18:17** And-they-took Avshalom and-cast him in-the-forest into the-pit the-great, and-raised over-him a-heap of-stones great very. And-all Yisra'el fled, each-man to-his-tent [le-ohalav].

**18:18** And-Avshalom had-taken and-raised for-himself in-his-life the-pillar [mattsevet] that [is] in-[the]-Valley of-the-King, for he-said, "I-have no son to-cause-to-remember [lehazkir] my-name." And-he-called the-pillar by-his-name, and-it-is-called "Hand [yad] of-Avshalom" unto this day.

**18:19** And-Achimaats son of-Tsadoq said, "Let-me-run, please, and-I-will-bear-tidings [avasserah] [to]-the-king, that YHWH has-vindicated-him [shepato] from-[the]-hand of-his-enemies."

**18:20** And-said to-him Yo'av, "Not a-man of-tidings [besorah] [are]-you this day, but-you-will-bear-tidings on-another day. And-this day you-will-not bear-tidings, because [al-ken] the-son of-the-king is-dead."

**18:21** And-said Yo'av to-the-Cushite [la-Kushi], "Go, tell the-king what you-have-seen." And-bowed the-Cushite to-Yo'av and-ran.

**18:22** And-again [vayyosef] Achimaats son of-Tsadoq said to Yo'av, "And-let-be what-may [yehi mah], let-me-run, please, also I, after the-Cushite." And-said Yo'av, "Why-is-this [are]-you running, my-son, and-to-you there-is-no tidings found [besorah motse'et]?"

**18:23** "And-let-be what-may, let-me-run." And-he-said to-him, "Run." And-ran Achimaats by-way of-the-plain [ha-kikkar] and-passed the-Cushite.

**18:24** And-David [was]-sitting between the-two gates. And-went the-watchman [ha-tsopheh] upon [the]-roof of-the-gate, upon the-wall, and-lifted his-eyes and-saw, and-behold, a-man running alone.

**18:25** And-called the-watchman and-told the-king. And-said the-king, "If alone, tidings [besorah] [are] in-his-mouth." And-he-came, going [halokh] and-drawing-near [qarev].

**18:26** And-saw the-watchman another man running, and-called the-watchman to the-gatekeeper and-said, "Behold, a-man running alone." And-said the-king, "Also this-one [is] bearing-tidings [mevasser]."

**18:27** And-said the-watchman, "I see the-running of-the-first as-[the]-running of-Achimaats son of-Tsadoq." And-said the-king, "A-good man [is]-this, and-with good tidings [besorah tovah] he-comes."

**18:28** And-called Achimaats and-said to the-king, "Peace [shalom]!" And-he-bowed to-the-king on-his-face to-the-ground. And-he-said, "Blessed [be]-YHWH your-God who has-delivered-up [sigger] the-men who lifted their-hand against-my-lord the-king."

**18:29** And-said the-king, "Is-there-peace [ha-shalom] for-the-youth, for-Avshalom?" And-said Achimaats, "I-saw the-great tumult [ha-hamon ha-gadol] when-sent [the]-servant of-the-king, [even] Yo'av, and-your-servant, and-I-did-not know what [it was]."

**18:30** And-said the-king, "Turn-around, stand here." And-he-turned-around and-stood.

**18:31** And-behold, the-Cushite came. And-said the-Cushite, "Let-receive-tidings [yitbasser] my-lord the-king, for YHWH has-vindicated-you [shepatkha] this-day from-[the]-hand of-all who-rose-up against-you."

**18:32** And-said the-king to the-Cushite, "Is-there-peace [ha-shalom] for-the-youth, for-Avshalom?" And-said the-Cushite, "Let-be as-the-youth [the]-enemies of-my-lord the-king and-all who rose-up against-you for-evil [le-ra'ah]."

**18:33** And-was-shaken [vayyirgaz] the-king, and-went-up to the-upper-chamber [aliyyat] of-the-gate and-wept. And-thus he-said in-his-going: "My-son Avshalom! My-son, my-son Avshalom! Who-will-give [mi-yitten] my-dying, I, instead-of-you! Avshalom my-son, my-son!"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.5 — le'at li la-na'ar le-Avshalom:** David's plea uses three lamed-prepositions: *le'at* (gently), *li* (for my sake), *la-na'ar* (with the young man), *le-Avshalom* (Absalom). The word *le'at* means "softly, gently" — David is begging his generals to show mercy to his rebel son.

**v.8 — vayyerev ha-ya'ar:** "The forest consumed more" — the verb אכל (to eat/devour) is used of the forest itself, as if it were a predatory force. The forest of Ephraim becomes a character in the narrative, killing more than the sword.

**v.9 — vayyechezeq ro'sho va-elah:** "His head was caught in the oak." The MT says specifically *ro'sho* (his head), not his hair. The tradition that Absalom was caught by his hair comes from combining this verse with the description of his hair in 14:26, but the text itself says "head."

**v.14 — shevatim:** The word שְׁבָטִים can mean "rods, staves, tribes, scepters." Here it refers to wooden shafts or staves — not the polished darts of later English translations. Joab thrusts them into Absalom's living body.

**v.18 — mattsevet:** Absalom's pillar (*mattsevet*) in the King's Valley is his attempt to create a memorial. The irony: he who sought to replace his father's *name* (shem) is memorialized only by a stone, while the cairn of shame (v.17) marks his actual burial.

**v.33 — mi-yitten muti ani takhtekha:** "Who will give my dying, I, instead of you" — the *mi-yitten* construction expresses an impossible wish. David does not say "I wish I had died" but uses the more agonizing formulation: "Who will grant that I might die in your place?" The fivefold repetition of *beni* (my son) in the Hebrew is unparalleled in its raw grief.

*— EMET*
